note: Fifty synthetic headline + article pairs, every entity fictional. Scored every run in full-text mode; the first scoring run writes baseline.json and later runs report agreement against it. `expected` is the authoring intent for reading drift, not a ground truth the model is graded on.

items.headline: Marlow council approves 2% water rate increase starting in March
items.article: The Marlow city council voted 6-1 on Tuesday to raise residential water rates by 2 percent beginning March 1. Council members said the increase covers rising treatment costs and a pump replacement at the Elm Street plant. The lone dissenter, councillor Pat Reyes, argued the increase should be delayed until a rate study is complete. The change adds about $1.40 to the average monthly bill, according to the utility department.

items.headline: Vexa Corp to cut 400 jobs as it closes its Dayton plant
items.article: Vexa Corp said Monday it will close its Dayton manufacturing plant by the end of the year, eliminating about 400 positions. The company said production will move to its facility in Reno, where it has added two assembly lines. Affected workers will receive severance and may apply for roles at other sites, a spokesperson said. The plant opened in 1987 and makes industrial valves.

items.headline: Study finds commuters who cycle report better sleep than drivers
items.article: A study of 3,200 adults published Wednesday in the Journal of Urban Health found that people who commute by bicycle reported better sleep quality than those who drive, after adjusting for age, income and work hours. The authors cautioned that the design cannot show cycling causes better sleep, and that people who already sleep well may be more likely to cycle. The effect was modest, about half a point on a ten-point scale.

items.headline: Storm leaves 12,000 without power across Harlan County
items.article: About 12,000 customers in Harlan County were without electricity Thursday morning after overnight winds brought down lines and trees, the Harlan Power Cooperative said. Crews expected to restore most service by evening, with some rural areas waiting until Friday. No injuries were reported. Two schools closed for the day.

items.headline: Riverton Library extends weekend hours after pilot draws record visits
items.article: Riverton Public Library will keep its main branch open until 8 p.m. on Saturdays and Sundays starting next month, the library board announced. A six-week pilot of the later hours drew the highest weekend attendance in the library's records, with visits up 38 percent over the same period last year. The board approved $62,000 in additional staffing to make the change permanent.

items.headline: Senator Ortiz introduces bill to cap overdraft fees at $5
items.article: Senator Dana Ortiz introduced legislation on Tuesday that would cap bank overdraft fees at $5 per transaction and limit them to one per day. The bill has four co-sponsors and faces an uncertain path in committee, where a similar measure stalled last year. Banking groups said the cap would push institutions to stop offering overdraft protection entirely. Consumer advocates welcomed the bill.

items.headline: Northfield Dolphins win regional title in overtime, 24-21
items.article: The Northfield Dolphins defeated the Ashby Hawks 24-21 in overtime on Friday to win the regional championship, their first since 2014. Kicker Sam Oduya hit a 38-yard field goal to end the game after both teams traded touchdowns in regulation. The Dolphins advance to the state semifinal next Saturday.

items.headline: Tolland raises minimum wage to $16 an hour from January
items.article: Tolland's minimum wage will rise to $16 an hour on January 1 under a schedule the legislature approved three years ago. The increase is the final step of a phased plan that began at $12. State labor officials estimate about 90,000 workers will see a raise. Employers must post the new rate by December 15.

items.headline: Airline Kestrel cancels 60 flights as pilots' sickout enters second day
items.article: Kestrel Airways cancelled 60 flights on Wednesday, the second day of what the airline called an unofficial sickout by pilots during contract talks. The pilots' union denied organizing the absences but said members were frustrated by the pace of negotiations. Kestrel said it was rebooking affected passengers and expected further cancellations Thursday.

items.headline: Museum returns 17th-century manuscript to Kolvar after decade-long claim
items.article: The Halden Museum formally returned a 17th-century illuminated manuscript to the Republic of Kolvar on Monday, ending a claim Kolvar first filed in 2016. The museum's board concluded last year that the manuscript had been removed from a Kolvar monastery during the 1890s occupation. A Kolvar delegation accepted the manuscript at a ceremony in Halden.

items.headline: Brightwater reports third straight quarter of losses, shares fall 9%
items.article: Brightwater Energy posted a net loss of $41 million for the third quarter, its third consecutive quarterly loss, as lower wholesale prices offset higher output. Shares fell 9 percent in early trading. The company reaffirmed its full-year guidance and said two new storage projects would come online in the spring.

items.headline: Health department confirms 14 measles cases in Greaves County
items.article: The Greaves County health department confirmed 14 measles cases as of Friday, up from nine a week earlier. All but two of the cases are in unvaccinated children, officials said. Free vaccination clinics will run at three schools next week. The department urged anyone with symptoms to call ahead before visiting a clinic.

items.headline: Caldera volcano alert level lowered after two quiet weeks
items.article: The national geological survey lowered the alert level for the Caldera volcano from orange to yellow on Monday after two weeks without significant tremors or gas emissions. The exclusion zone around the summit remains in place. Scientists said the volcano could still erupt with little warning and that monitoring would continue at the same intensity.

items.headline: Ferry service to Port Ellis suspended through weekend for hull repairs
items.article: The Port Ellis ferry will not run from Friday through Sunday while the vessel undergoes hull repairs, the transit authority said. A replacement bus will run between the terminals on an hourly schedule. Normal service is expected to resume Monday morning.

items.headline: Court orders Pinecrest to restore bus routes cut in June
items.article: A district court on Thursday ordered the city of Pinecrest to restore three bus routes it eliminated in June, finding the city had not completed the public review required under its own transit ordinance. The city said it would comply while it considers an appeal. The routes served about 2,000 riders a day.

items.headline: Lakeshore teachers ratify contract with 4% raise
items.article: Members of the Lakeshore Education Association voted 812 to 96 on Wednesday to ratify a three-year contract that includes a 4 percent raise in the first year and 3 percent in each of the following two. The school board is expected to approve the agreement next week. The contract also adds two planning days to the calendar.

items.headline: Drought forces Alder Valley farms to leave a third of fields fallow
items.article: Farmers in the Alder Valley will leave roughly a third of their irrigated acreage unplanted this season after the irrigation district cut water allocations to 40 percent of normal, the district said. The cut follows a third consecutive dry winter. Growers of lower-value crops are expected to be hit hardest.

items.headline: Pollster says Weston mayoral race is a dead heat two weeks out
items.article: A poll of 600 likely voters released Monday shows incumbent mayor Ira Chen and challenger Lena Park tied at 44 percent each, with 12 percent undecided, two weeks before the Weston election. The poll's margin of error is 4 points. Both campaigns said the result matched their internal numbers.

items.headline: Crime in Belmont rose 15% last year
items.article: Reported crime in Belmont rose 15 percent in 2025 compared with 2024, according to figures released by the police department. The department attributed most of the increase to a new online reporting system that made it easier to report minor property offenses. Violent crime fell 6 percent over the same period, continuing a five-year decline.

items.headline: Half of Carrow Hospital's nurses say they plan to quit
items.article: Half of the 120 nurses who answered a union survey at Carrow Hospital said they were considering leaving within two years, the union said. The hospital employs about 900 nurses; the survey was distributed online and respondents were self-selected. Hospital management said its own exit data shows turnover near the regional average.

items.headline: Mayor's travel costs tripled this year
items.article: Travel spending by the mayor's office rose to $38,000 this year from $12,000 last year, city records show. The increase reflects two trade missions that the city council approved and funded in advance, including a delegation to a sister city that had been postponed twice during the pandemic. The office's overall budget fell 3 percent.

items.headline: New drug cuts migraine days by 50%
items.article: A phase 3 trial of the migraine drug velanzumab found that patients had about 50 percent fewer monthly migraine days than at baseline. Patients receiving a placebo saw a 35 percent reduction, so the drug's effect over placebo was roughly 1.5 fewer days a month. The trial was funded by the drug's manufacturer. Side effects were mostly mild.

items.headline: Ashford schools rank last in the state in reading
items.article: Ashford's fourth-grade reading scores were the lowest among the state's 48 districts on this year's assessment, the education department reported. The district's scores rose nine points from last year, the largest gain in the state, and the superintendent noted that Ashford has the highest share of students learning English. The district adopted a new reading curriculum two years ago.

items.headline: Oakhurst dam declared unsafe
items.article: State inspectors rated the Oakhurst dam 'unsatisfactory' in a routine review, the lowest of four condition ratings, citing seepage at the eastern abutment. The rating does not indicate imminent failure, the report said; it requires the owner to submit a repair plan within 90 days. The reservoir has been kept 10 feet below its normal level since the spring as a precaution.

items.headline: Tech firm Lumen pays no corporate tax for third year
items.article: Lumen Systems paid no corporate income tax for the third consecutive year, its annual report shows, after applying credits for research spending and losses carried forward from a 2021 restructuring. The company paid $84 million in payroll and property taxes. Its research credit claims are under routine review by the tax authority.

items.headline: Fenwick bridge closed after inspection
items.article: The Fenwick Road bridge was closed to trucks over 10 tons on Tuesday after an inspection found corrosion on two support beams, the county said. Cars and light vehicles may continue to use the bridge. Repairs are scheduled for the spring, and the county said the restriction is precautionary.

items.headline: Unemployment in Dorne hits 6.1%
items.article: Dorne's unemployment rate rose to 6.1 percent in October from 5.8 percent in September, the labor office said. The rise came as 4,000 more people entered the labor force to look for work; the number of people employed also rose, by 2,500. Economists said the figures were consistent with a growing economy drawing people back into the job market.

items.headline: Thousands protest Norwood housing plan
items.article: About 2,000 people marched through Norwood on Saturday against a plan to build 600 apartments on the former rail yard, police estimated. A counter-demonstration of roughly 300 people supporting the plan gathered at city hall. A city survey in August found 54 percent of residents in favor of the development and 31 percent opposed.

items.headline: Governor Hale took bribes from road contractor, report says
items.article: A report by the state auditor says a road contractor made payments to a consulting firm owned by Governor Hale's brother while bidding on highway work. The report does not say the governor received money and makes no finding of bribery. Hale called the report a political attack and said he had no involvement in his brother's business. The contractor's attorney said the payments were for legitimate consulting work.

items.headline: Factory leak poisoned town's water, residents say
items.article: Residents of Millbrook told a public meeting Thursday that a chemical leak at the Arden Chemical plant contaminated the town's wells. State testing of the wells found solvent levels below the legal limit, and the plant denies any leak occurred. A university team is conducting independent sampling, with results expected next month. Residents cited skin rashes and a chemical smell.

items.headline: Coach Diaz fired for berating players
items.article: Westlake University dismissed head coach Ruben Diaz on Monday. The athletic director said only that the program was going in a new direction. Two former players told the student newspaper that Diaz routinely screamed at athletes; three current players disputed that account and said he was demanding but fair. Diaz said through his agent that he was not told why he was let go.

items.headline: Stadium deal will cost taxpayers $300 million
items.article: A city-commissioned analysis estimates the proposed stadium financing package would cost taxpayers $300 million over 30 years. The team's own study puts the net cost near zero after projected tax revenue from the surrounding development. Independent economists have questioned both figures. The council votes next week.

items.headline: Police shot unarmed man, family says
items.article: The family of a man shot by Harbor City police on Friday said he was unarmed, citing a witness. Police said officers recovered a handgun at the scene and that the man had pointed it at them. Body camera footage has not been released; the district attorney's office said it is reviewing the recordings. The man is in stable condition.

items.headline: Vexa knew about defect before recall, lawsuit claims
items.article: A lawsuit filed Tuesday alleges Vexa Corp learned of a valve defect eight months before it issued a recall. Vexa said it recalled the valves within weeks of confirming the problem and called the allegation baseless. The suit cites internal emails the plaintiffs' lawyers have not made public. A judge has not yet ruled on whether the case can proceed.

items.headline: Wind farm killed 200 birds, group says
items.article: A conservation group says its volunteers counted 200 dead birds beneath turbines at the Ridgeback wind farm over the past year. The farm's operator said its own monitoring, conducted by a licensed consultant, found 31 fatalities over the same period and that the group's count likely included birds killed by other causes. State wildlife officials have not reviewed either count.

items.headline: Eastbrook school board member resigns amid plagiarism scandal
items.article: Eastbrook school board member Tom Vance resigned Tuesday, saying he wanted to spend more time with his family. His resignation came a week after a blog accused him of copying passages of his campaign platform from another candidate. Vance has said the overlap came from a shared consultant and denied plagiarism. The other candidate has not commented.

items.headline: Kestrel Airways to be acquired by Meridian for $2 billion
items.article: Kestrel Airways is in talks to be acquired by Meridian Air Group, according to two people familiar with the discussions who spoke on condition of anonymity. The people said a deal could value Kestrel at around $2 billion but cautioned that talks could still fall apart. Neither company would comment.

items.headline: Oakhurst bank robbery suspect arrested
items.article: Police in Oakhurst said Wednesday they had detained a person of interest in connection with Monday's robbery of the First Oakhurst Bank. The person has not been charged, and police declined to say whether they believe the individual took part in the robbery. The investigation is continuing.

items.headline: Lumen Systems to lay off 2,000 workers
items.article: Lumen Systems is preparing to cut as many as 2,000 jobs in the coming months, a person briefed on the plans said, adding that the final number has not been decided and could be considerably lower. The company said it does not comment on speculation. Lumen employs about 30,000 people.

items.headline: Train derailment caused by faulty brakes
items.article: Investigators have begun examining the braking system of the freight train that derailed near Colby on Sunday, the transportation safety board said. The board said it was too early to identify a cause and that track conditions, speed and the brakes were all being reviewed. A preliminary report is expected within 30 days.

items.headline: Fire at Arden plant started by arson
items.article: Fire officials said the cause of Tuesday's fire at the Arden Chemical plant remains under investigation. A plant employee told a local radio station she believed the fire had been set deliberately, but officials said they had found no evidence of arson so far and were also examining an electrical panel in the area where the fire began.

items.headline: Senator Ortiz to retire at end of term
items.article: Senator Dana Ortiz has told several allies she is leaning toward not seeking re-election, according to three people who have spoken with her, though they said she has not made a final decision. Her office said the senator would announce her plans early next year and that any report of a decision was premature.

items.headline: Caldera eruption imminent, scientists warn
items.article: Scientists monitoring the Caldera volcano said Thursday that a recent increase in tremors could indicate rising magma but stressed that such activity has subsided without an eruption many times before. The alert level was unchanged. 'We cannot say whether or when it will erupt,' the survey's director said.

items.headline: Marlow council votes to double water rates
items.article: The Marlow city council voted 6-1 on Tuesday to raise residential water rates by 2 percent beginning March 1. Council members said the increase covers rising treatment costs and a pump replacement at the Elm Street plant. The change adds about $1.40 to the average monthly bill, according to the utility department.

items.headline: Study proves cycling to work cures insomnia
items.article: A study of 3,200 adults found that people who commute by bicycle reported slightly better sleep quality than those who drive. The authors cautioned that the design cannot show cycling causes better sleep, and that people who already sleep well may be more likely to cycle. The effect was modest, about half a point on a ten-point scale. Insomnia was not assessed.

items.headline: Governor Hale indicted in bribery scheme
items.article: A report by the state auditor says a road contractor made payments to a consulting firm owned by Governor Hale's brother while bidding on highway work. The report does not say the governor received money, makes no finding of wrongdoing by the governor, and has not been referred to prosecutors. No charges have been filed against anyone.

items.headline: Measles outbreak closes every school in Greaves County
items.article: The Greaves County health department confirmed 14 measles cases as of Friday. One elementary school cancelled classes for a day to allow deep cleaning; all other schools in the county remained open. The department said closures were not currently warranted and urged vaccination.

items.headline: Brightwater posts record profit as shares surge
items.article: Brightwater Energy posted a net loss of $41 million for the third quarter, its third consecutive quarterly loss, as lower wholesale prices offset higher output. Shares fell 9 percent in early trading. The company reaffirmed its full-year guidance.

items.headline: Pinecrest to eliminate all bus service after court ruling
items.article: A district court on Thursday ordered the city of Pinecrest to restore three bus routes it eliminated in June. The city said it would comply while it considers an appeal. The city's remaining 22 routes were never affected by the case and continue to operate on their normal schedules.

items.headline: Tolland slashes minimum wage for young workers
items.article: Tolland's minimum wage will rise to $16 an hour on January 1 for all workers, including those under 20, under a schedule the legislature approved three years ago. A proposal to create a lower training wage for teenagers was rejected in committee in 2024 and has not been reintroduced.
